selected.analysis_type: repeated-measures multi-level time, stratified by sex
selected.formula: ~ subject + time (fitted separately within each sex)

decisions.reason: The abstract reports acute responses separately for females and males, before and after training, so sex is a stratum and each sex gets one model on all its time points with subject blocking. T1 vs T3 is the GEO-summary training effect at rest. The sex x exercise interaction (315 transcripts) and the training x acute interaction are not run: interaction contrasts are not expressible as pairwise level comparisons in the runner, and the abstract does not give their model. Other pairwise comparisons the suitability report lists (e.g. T4 vs T1) are not paper contrasts.

caveats: Comparison with the paper rests on the PubMed abstract and GEO summary only; no full text.
Time-point coding 1-4 is inferred as chronological (pre/post acute, pre/post training); GEO does not define it.
Paper's DE method unknown; DESeq2 with subject blocking used instead.
Sex x exercise interaction (315 transcripts) not reproduced.

Contradicts the paper: the paper reports the acute response attenuated after training in both sexes (F 5,135 -> 94; M 567 -> 165). Here females attenuate (5,780 -> 427 at FDR<0.1) but males increase (217 -> 601), so the male attenuation is not reproduced with DESeq2 ~ subject + time.
Pre-training females match the paper well (5,780 vs 5,135); GSEA shows OXIDATIVE_PHOSPHORYLATION up in females, in line with the abstract's 'oxidative metabolism' pathways in females.

decisions.reason: Counts from the abstract (acute) and the GEO summary (training at baseline, 'FDR>0.1' i.e. none). Abstract names no genes.
